mcqs.q: The graph shows how the intensity I of the light on a screen varies with position x in a Young's double-slit experiment. The two slits are 0.40 mm apart and each is 0.020 mm wide; the screen is 2.0 m from the slits, and monochromatic light is incident normally on them. What is the wavelength of the light?
mcqs.specStatementText: Young’s double-slit interference as given by s = λD/d where s is the separation of fringes, d is the separation of the slits, and D is the distance from the slits to the screen.
mcqs.explain: Adjacent maxima on the graph are 3.0 mm apart, so s = 3.0 × 10⁻³ m. Rearranging s = λD/d gives λ = sd/D = (3.0 × 10⁻³ × 0.40 × 10⁻³)/2.0 = 6.0 × 10⁻⁷ m, orange light of 600 nm.
mcqs.working: From the graph, adjacent maxima are at x = 0, 3, 6 mm, so the fringe separation is s = 3.0 mm = 3.0 × 10⁻³ m. s = λD/d ⇒ λ = sd/D = (3.0 × 10⁻³ m × 0.40 × 10⁻³ m)/2.0 m = 6.0 × 10⁻⁷ m (600 nm).
rationales: Adjacent maxima on the graph are 3.0 mm apart, so s = 3.0 × 10⁻³ m. Rearranging s = λD/d gives λ = sd/D = (3.0 × 10⁻³ × 0.40 × 10⁻³)/2.0 = 6.0 × 10⁻⁷ m, orange light of 600 nm.
This divides the 12 mm between the outermost maxima by the five maxima counted, giving 2.4 mm. There are only four fringe spacings between five maxima, so s = 12/4 = 3.0 mm and λ = 6.0 × 10⁻⁷ m.

This uses the slit width, 0.020 mm, in place of the slit separation. The fringe separation s = λD/d depends on the distance d between the centres of the slits, 0.40 mm, giving λ = 6.0 × 10⁻⁷ m. The slit width affects only the brightness envelope.

This substitutes s = 3.0 (millimetres) alongside d in metres and D in metres. All lengths must be in the same unit: s = 3.0 × 10⁻³ m gives λ = 6.0 × 10⁻⁷ m. A wavelength of 0.6 mm would be far into the infrared, not visible light.

mcqs.q: The graph shows the intensity pattern produced on a distant screen when monochromatic light is incident normally on two rectangular slits of width b whose centres are a distance d apart. The dashed line is the single-slit diffraction envelope. What is the value of the ratio d/b?
mcqs.specStatementText: that the single-slit pattern modulates the double slit interference pattern
mcqs.explain: The envelope's first minimum (θ = λ/b) coincides with the position of the missing 4th-order fringe (θ = 4λ/d). Equating them, λ/b = 4λ/d, so d/b = 4: the slit separation is four times the slit width.
mcqs.working: Interference maxima occur at sin θ ≈ θ = nλ/d; the single-slit envelope has its first minimum at θ = λ/b. On the graph the envelope falls to zero exactly where the 4th-order fringe would be (the central lobe holds orders 0, ±1, ±2, ±3 and the ±4 fringes are missing), so 4λ/d = λ/b, giving d/b = 4.
rationales: This takes θ = λ/b to be the whole width of the central envelope, which spans eight fringe spacings (from the missing −4 to the missing +4). λ/b is the half-width, from the centre to the first minimum, which is four fringe spacings: 4λ/d = λ/b and d/b = 4.

This counts the seven bright fringes inside the central lobe and takes its half-width as 3.5 fringe spacings. The half-width is set by where the envelope reaches zero, which is where the 4th fringe would be, four fringe spacings from the centre, so d/b = 4.

This swaps the roles of b and d, taking the fringe spacing to be λ/b and the envelope half-width λ/d. The narrow fringes come from the slit separation d and the broad envelope from the slit width b, so the ratio is d/b = 4, not 1/4.
The envelope's first minimum (θ = λ/b) coincides with the position of the missing 4th-order fringe (θ = 4λ/d). Equating them, λ/b = 4λ/d, so d/b = 4: the slit separation is four times the slit width.

A solid curve of narrow, equally spaced interference fringes sits under a dashed single-slit envelope, labelled dashed: single-slit envelope. The central lobe of the envelope contains a tall central fringe and three fringes on each side of it, each weaker than the last; the envelope reaches zero where the fourth fringe on each side would be, and that fringe is absent. Beyond, on each side, a much lower secondary lobe of the envelope contains two further faint fringes before the graph ends.
